subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'pedal' (or pedal point) in texture is:
options: A sustained or repeated note, often in the bass, held under changing harmonies
questions.explain: A pedal is a held or repeated note, usually in the bass, that continues while harmonies change above it.

questions.q: When performing in an ensemble, watching a conductor or leader mainly helps players to:
options: Stay together in time and respond to changes
questions.explain: Following a conductor or leader keeps the ensemble together in time and unified in expression.

questions.q: In a DAW, 'automation' is most commonly used to:
options: Make settings like volume or panning change automatically over time
questions.explain: Automation lets parameters such as volume or panning change automatically across a track over time.

questions.q: Two quavers together are worth the same as one:
questions.explain: Two quavers equal one crotchet beat.

questions.q: In the mnemonic 'MAD T-SHIRT' for the elements of music, what does the 'I' stand for?
questions.explain: In 'MAD T-SHIRT' the I stands for instrumentation, meaning the choice of instruments and voices used.

questions.q: What does a natural sign do?
options: Cancels a previous sharp or flat
Lowers a note by a tone
Raises a note by a tone
questions.explain: A natural cancels a sharp or flat, returning the note to its natural pitch.

questions.q: How many beats does a crotchet last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A crotchet lasts one beat in 4/4 time.

questions.q: In the circle of fifths, how many sharps are in the key signature of D major?
questions.explain: D major has two sharps (F sharp and C sharp) in its key signature.

questions.q: In music, what does the dynamic marking 'forte' (f) mean?
questions.explain: Forte is an Italian dynamic term meaning loud, while piano means quiet.

questions.q: What does a 'coda' provide at the end of a composition?
options: A concluding section that rounds off the piece
questions.explain: A coda is a concluding section added to round off and finish a piece of music.

questions.q: Samba music originates from which country?
questions.explain: Samba is a lively percussion-driven music and dance from Brazil.

questions.q: A texture described as 'monophonic' has:
options: A single melodic line with no accompaniment
questions.explain: Monophonic texture is a single unaccompanied melodic line.

questions.q: Which clef is also known as the G clef and is used for higher-pitched instruments?
questions.explain: The treble (G) clef curls around the G line and is used for higher pitches.

questions.q: What is 'syncopation'?
options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.

questions.q: In vocal technique, 'vibrato' is:
options: A slight, regular wavering of pitch to enrich the tone
questions.explain: Vibrato is a slight, regular variation in pitch that adds warmth to a sustained note.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'accent' (>) tells a performer to:
options: Hold the note longer than written
questions.explain: An accent mark instructs the player to stress or emphasise that note.

questions.q: What does 'rit.' (ritardando) mean?
questions.explain: Ritardando means to gradually slow the tempo down.

questions.q: The harmonic minor scale differs from the natural minor by raising which note?
questions.explain: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh note by a semitone, creating a leading note.

questions.q: Which cadence ends on chord V, sounding unfinished?
questions.explain: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V and sounds incomplete.

questions.q: Using repetition when developing a musical idea helps to:
options: Make ideas memorable and give a sense of unity
questions.explain: Repetition makes musical ideas memorable and gives a piece unity and coherence.

questions.q: In a melody-and-accompaniment texture, the accompaniment:
options: Supports the melody with chords or a bass line
questions.explain: The accompaniment supports the main melody, often with chords or a bass line.

questions.q: 'Transposition' means:
options: Moving music up or down to a different pitch or key
Changing the dynamics of a piece
questions.explain: Transposition moves a piece of music to a higher or lower pitch (a different key).
